source.title: Jumping to Conclusions About the Beads Task? A Meta-analysis of Delusional Ideation and Data-Gathering

confidence_rationale: A rigorous meta-analysis of the 'jumping to conclusions' (JTC) data-gathering bias -- the cleanest candidate operationalisation of premature-collapse / anti-epistemic over-hasty inference. It confirms a real association between delusional ideation and reduced data-gathering BUT finds the effect modest and partly confounded (e.g. by general cognitive ability), which tempers any clean claim that 'premature hypothesis collapse' is a unitary, strongly-measurable failure mode. Direction is therefore mixed: supports the failure mode's reality, weakens its purity. Confidence 0.62 reflects strong source quality offset by the qualifying finding.
failure_signatures: Premature-collapse / anti-epistemic-panic: delusion-prone individuals gather less evidence before committing to a belief (fewer 'draws to decision') -- the over-hasty-inference signature INF-7 must track -- but the effect is small and confounded, so the failure mode is real yet not cleanly separable.
Cautions INF-7 against treating each register entry as a crisp dissociable mechanism: the clinical operationalisation of 'collapse too early' is noisier than the conceptual taxonomy implies.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across studies using the beads/draws-to-decision task, delusional and delusion-prone individuals gather less data before deciding (the JTC bias). Meta-analysis confirms the association is reliable but of modest magnitude and partly attributable to confounds such as general cognitive ability, rather than a large, specific reasoning deficit.
mapping.ree_translation: Operationalises and partly validates the INF-7 register's 'hypothesis collapse too early' / 'anti-epistemic panic' modes and maps them onto MECH-126 uncertainty collapse: committing on too little evidence = treating residual uncertainty as zero. But the modest, confounded effect size is the honest counter-weight: it supports including premature-collapse in the register while warning that the failure modes are graded and overlapping, not crisp dissociable lesions -- which is precisely why Q-070 is framed as an open question (do they reduce to the existing taxonomy?) rather than an assertion of a new parallel one.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The beads task is a narrow, abstract probabilistic-reasoning paradigm in humans; generalising 'draws to decision' to REE's epistemic-action-pressure / commitment-timing dynamics is a real stretch (no shared task, species, or substrate). It grounds the EXISTENCE and clinical relevance of an over-hasty-commitment failure mode and supplies a calibration warning, not a mechanism REE inherits.
mapping.source_context: Meta-analysis of human behavioural studies (beads / draws-to-decision probabilistic-reasoning task) in delusional and delusion-prone samples.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (meta-analysis). Lower mapping fidelity and higher transfer risk: abstract human reasoning task -> REE commitment timing; the modest/confounded effect is itself the evidentiary nuance, hence direction=mixed.
